## How the Day Unfolds

Departure from the hotel at 08:00. There are 2 possible schedules, depending on the distance to the dive site:

| Stage | Nearby-site schedule | Distant-site schedule |
|---|---|---|
| Arrival, 30-minute check dive | 09:30 | 10:30 |
| First dive: 18–25 m, maximum 1 hour | 10:30 | 11:30 |
| Start of 1.5-hour surface interval, snack | 11:30 | 12:30 |
| Second dive: 18–20 m, maximum 1 hour | 12:45 | 13:45 |
| Lunch and return journey | 13:45 | 14:45 |
| Arrival at the dive center | 15:15 | 16:30 |

## Dive Boat L/P El Galapago I

A fiberglass boat, 10 m long and 3 m wide. On board are 2 YAMAHA engines rated at 200 hp each, HF radio, EPIRB, GPS and O2. Capacity: 10 passengers, 2 guides, a captain and a sailor. There is a toilet.

## Choosing the Route

| Day of the week | Dive sites |
|---|---|
| Monday | FLOREANA (2 dives) |
| Tuesday | GORDON (2 dives) *** |
| Wednesday | NORTH MOSQUERA/ SEYMOUR CHANNEL |
| Thursday | BARTOLOME/COUSINS |
| Friday | SOUTH MOSQUERA/ DAPHNE |
| Saturday | SEYMOUR NORTHEAST / SEYMOUR CHANNEL |
| Sunday | PLAZAS/ GORDON*** |

The route may change at the discretion of the national park or due to circumstances beyond the dive center’s control. All sites listed below are possible options; a visit to each site is not guaranteed on a short program. Santa Fe and Punta Carrion are described in the Word document, but no fixed day of the week is specified for them.

## Bartolomé / Bartolome

Location: East of Santiago Island, this small island is known for its famous Bartolomé summit. The dive sites are an hour and a half by boat from Itabaca Channel (on the north side of Santa Cruz Island).

Conditions: Moderate current. At a depth of approximately 10 meters there is a platform inhabited by a variety of reef fish. Along the edge of the platform, underwater rocks begin at around 15 meters, offering a good chance of spotting pelagic species.

Marine life: Whitetip reef sharks, reef fish, barracudas, turtles, rays and a variety of invertebrates.

## Cousins / Cousins Rock

Location: Northeast of Santiago Island, near Bartolomé Island. The dive sites are an hour and a half by boat from Itabaca Channel (on the north side of Santa Cruz Island).

Conditions: Strong currents are usually absent here. The dive follows partly a reef and partly a wall, where endemic black coral can be found.

Marine life: Seahorses, barracudas, sea lions, Galápagos sharks, whitetip reef sharks, turtles, reef fish, eagle rays and a variety of invertebrates. Penguins may be spotted at the surface.

## Daphne / Daphne

Location: North of Santa Cruz Island, a bare rock with one dive site, 30 minutes from Itabaca Channel (on the north side of Santa Cruz Island).

Conditions: Strong currents are usually absent here; the bottom is rocky and sandy.

Marine life: A small cave (this is NOT a cave dive) where reef sharks rest, along with an underwater rock where many rays, Galápagos sharks, turtles, coral-reef fish and barracudas can be encountered. There are walls of black coral and numerous invertebrates.

## Floreana / Floreana

Location: South of Santa Cruz Island, with 3 possible dive sites: Punta Cormorant, Champion and Enderby. They are an hour and a half by boat from the dive center.

Conditions: Average depth of 18 meters. Strong currents are usually absent. This is a reef dive site where corals and sponges can be found.

Marine life: Sea lions, Galápagos sharks, whitetip reef sharks, turtles, reef fish, stingrays, eagle rays, barracudas and a variety of invertebrates.

## Gordon Rocks / Gordon Rocks

(Minimum experience required: 25 logged dives or a prior assessment by our dive guides at another site.)

Location: North of Santa Cruz Island, with 2 dive sites located 30 minutes from Itabaca Channel (on the north side of Santa Cruz Island).

Conditions: This rock formation is world-renowned among intermediate and advanced divers because of its strong currents and waves.

Marine life: Hammerhead sharks, Galápagos sharks, whitetip reef sharks, mobula rays, turtles, reef fish, stingrays, eagle rays, Galápagos eels, barracudas and a variety of invertebrates.

## Punta Carrion / Punta Carrion

Location: A prominent point in the northeast of Santa Cruz. This rocky formation extends to a depth of more than 30 meters and has fallen rocks due to erosion. The inner part of its north side forms a channel separating Santa Cruz from Baltra Island. The channel is 12–14 meters deep and is the calmest and safest place for diving.

Conditions: Depending on the wind, the eastern side can be somewhat choppy, with weak to moderate currents. It is a good place to encounter thermoclines rich in nutrients.

Marine life: Whitetip sharks, stingrays, eagle rays, marbled fish, scorpionfish, turtles and sea lions; schools of reef fish such as grunts (Haemulidae).

## North Mosquera / Mosquera Norte

Location: North of Santa Cruz Island, between North Seymour Island and Baltra Island. This is a small island rising out of the sea (a sandbar), with a dive site 25 minutes from Itabaca Channel (on the north side of Santa Cruz Island).

Conditions: Strong currents are usually absent. A sandy bottom at 10 meters is home to garden eels and pelagic species. North Mosquera is a sandy and rocky area connecting to Seymour Channel, with reef fish and resting "tintorera" sharks.

Marine life: Hammerhead sharks, Galápagos sharks, blacktip reef sharks, whitetip reef sharks, sea lions, turtles, barracudas, reef fish, eagle rays, mobula rays, Galápagos eels and a variety of invertebrates.

## South Mosquera / Mosquera Sur

Location: North of Santa Cruz Island, between the northern part of Seymour Island and Baltra Island. This small island rises out of the sea (a sandbar); the dive site is 25 minutes from Itabaca Channel (on the north side of Santa Cruz Island).

Conditions: Weak currents; a broad 5-meter reef with a sloping 18-meter ravine containing black corals and invertebrate mollusks. There is also an underwater canyon at a depth of 18 meters with pelagic species.

Marine life: Hammerhead sharks, blacktip reef sharks, whitetip reef sharks, sea lions, turtles, barracudas and reef life.

## Plazas / Plazas

Location: Off the eastern coast of Santa Cruz.

Conditions: Visitors are currently prohibited from going ashore on North Plaza, but diving off the back of North Plaza is a pleasant, easy and relaxing dive, with relatively little current or swell. Dives usually begin along the middle of the northern shore, where a gently sloping boulder field descends to the sandy bottom at a depth of approximately 24 m (80 ft). Whitetip reef sharks, marbled and diamond rays can be found here, while swaying fields of Galápagos garden eels inhabit sandy patches throughout the boulder slope.

Marine life: Most of the activity takes place within the first 14 m (45 ft). Huge schools of yellowtail surgeonfish, yellowtail mullet and numerous parrotfish inhabit the shallows. On the eastern side of the island you are more likely to see pelagic animals, including hammerhead and Galápagos sharks. This eastern point can be especially good during the warmer months (January–May), when cross-currents may bring manta rays, and even snorkelers may enjoy a long swim alongside these magnificent animals. Individual whale sharks occasionally visit during the hot season. Whether snorkeling or diving, sea lions are likely to become your constant companions.

## Santa Fe / Santa Fe

Location: Southeast of Santa Cruz Island, with 2 dive sites (1 hour by boat from our base).

Conditions: The water is usually clear and transparent, with gentle currents. Marine life is very diverse.

Marine life: Reef fish, stingrays, eagle rays, turtles, moray eels, sea lions, reef sharks and invertebrate mollusks.

## Seymour (Channel) / Seymur Canal

Location: North of Santa Cruz Island, with 2 dive sites situated 25 minutes from Itabaca Channel (on the north side of Santa Cruz Island).

Conditions: Suitable for divers of any level, although strong currents may occasionally occur. There are platform reefs with many fish species, a sandy bottom and a 10-meter reef home to numerous "tintorera" sharks.

Marine life: Sea lions, Galápagos sharks, reef sharks, hammerhead sharks, mobula rays, turtles, reef fish, eagle rays, Galápagos eels, barracudas and a variety of invertebrates.

## Seymour (Point) / Seymur Punta

Location: North of Santa Cruz Island, 30 minutes from Itabaca Channel (on the north side of Santa Cruz Island).

Conditions: This site is a little more challenging than Seymour Channel. The rocky seabed has small caves at a depth of 12 meters, where resting striped turtles and sharks may be found. The current can be somewhat strong. It is a mixed dive, starting near the shore and then moving into deeper water to look for pelagic animals. At the end of the dive there is a platform where sharks drift along with the current.

Marine life: Sea lions, Galápagos sharks, whitetip reef sharks, hammerhead sharks, mobula rays, turtles, reef fish, eagle rays, Galápagos eels, barracudas and a variety of invertebrates.

## Requirements for Participants

A diver certification (PADI, NAUI, CMAS or equivalent) is mandatory.

Complete the application form.

A medical certificate is required if any medical condition is declared and/or for people over 60 who have not dived in the last 8 months.

The minimum participation age is 12.

We accept certified beginner divers at all dive sites except Gordon Rocks. For Gordon Rocks, we require at least 25 logged dives in the past 18 months and an assessment by our dive guides during a dive at another site or during the check dive.

For divers without certification, we offer Discover Scuba Diving and PADI courses (please ask about the program).

We accept non-certified participants who accompany family members or go snorkeling, provided they pay the full price of the diving day.

For Gordon Rocks, different sections of the program state the requirements as "25 dives or a guide’s assessment" and "25 dives within 18 months and a guide’s assessment". The dive center confirms eligibility for this site before departure.

## Equipment and Conditions of the Entire P027 Program of the Entire P027 Program

The described group transfers, excursions and 2 dives on diving days;

Accommodation at Hotel Fiesta;

The stated meals: the meal plan includes breakfast and lunch every day; on departure day, only breakfast at the hotel;

Diving equipment: a 5–7 mm wetsuit, regulator, buoyancy compensator, mask, fins, boots, hood, fabric gloves, weights and 12-liter compressed-air tanks with valve systems;

English-speaking naturalist guide/divemaster throughout the excursions and dives.

Paid separately: DIN adapter ($5 each); NITROX tanks ($15 each); dive computer ($15 per day); tips.

## From the City to the Water and Forested Banks

We invite your team to [Gamboa](/panama/place/gamboa/) for a program lasting approximately 3 hours. You will set out on a boat expedition along the waters of the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/), then continue exploring Panama City.

On the seven-day corporate trip, we arrange departure from Hyatt Regency Panama City at 07:30 on a 45-seat bus, with up to 3 hours of waiting time for the group. A guide-coordinator assists with the departure, the subsequent city tour and lunch.

We will agree on the boat route and program details with you while planning the trip. Transportation, waiting time and accompanying services will be priced for your group.
